{{Short description|American mathematician topologist}}

'''Charles Livingston''' is a [[mathematician]] working in [[geometric topology]], [[low-dimensional topology]] and [[knot theory]]. He is a professor [[emeritus]] at [[Indiana University Bloomington|Indiana University]].<ref name="Quanta">{{citation|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/special-surfaces-remain-distinct-in-four-dimensions-20220616/|title=Surfaces So Different Even a Fourth Dimension Can't Make Them the Same|magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]]|date=16 June 2022|first=Kevin|last=Hartnett}}</ref>

In 1982, he posed a [[conjecture]] on [[Seifert surface]]s that remained open for 40 years. It was finally [[Mathematical proof|solved]] in 2022 in a collaborative effort of five mathematicians: Kyle Hayden, Seungwon Kim, [[Maggie Miller (mathematician)|Maggie Miller]], JungHwan Park, and Isaac Sundberg.<ref name="Quanta" />

His undergraduate studies were at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] and [[MIT]].<ref>[[Mathematical Association of America]], MathFest 2004, PRIZES and AWARDS, https://maa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/PRZBKmathfest2004.pdf</ref> Livingston obtained his PhD in 1980 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], advised by [[Robion Kirby]] (thesis: ''The Knotting of Surfaces in 4-Spaces'').<ref>[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]: https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=22697</ref>

He is the author of the textbook ''Knot Theory'' (MAA).<ref name="review1">Book review 1 (by [[Joan S. Birman]]) at ''[[The American Mathematical Monthly]]''): https://www.jstor.org/stable/2974659</ref><ref name="review2">Book review 2 (by [[W. B. R. Lickorish]]) at ''[[The Mathematical Gazette]]'': https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-gazette/article/abs/knot-theory-by-charles-livingston-pp-240-3150-1994-isbn-0883850273-mathematical-association-of-america/FA5EDC177114CA94B2AD3F9C213C0F07</ref> In 2004, he was awarded the [[Lester R. Ford Award]] from the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://maa.org/paul-r-halmos-lester-r-ford-awards/ | title=Paul R. Halmos – Lester R. Ford Awards – Mathematical Association of America }}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
===Research papers===
*"Surfaces bounding the unlink". ''[[Michigan Math. J.]]'', 29(3):289–298, 1982. (paper where he proposed his conjecture)
*with Paul Kirk: "Twisted Alexander invariants, Reidemeister torsion, and Casson–Gordon invariants", ''[[Topology (journal)|Topology]]'' 38 (3), 635–661
*"Computations of the Ozsváth–Szabó knot concordance invariant", ''[[Geometry & Topology]]'' 8 (2), 735–742
*"Heegaard Floer homology and rational cuspidal curves", ''[[Forum of Mathematics]]'', Sigma 2, e28
*"Twisted knot polynomials: inversion, mutation and concordance", ''Topology'' 38 (3), 663–671

===Textbooks===
*''Knot Theory'' (Mathematical Association of America Textbooks, Series Number 24)<ref name="review1" /><ref name="review2" />
